analysis: The change is documentation-only in docs/operations/provider-release.md. It re-describes the release routing: master pushes publish staging only (when STAGING_ENABLED is true), the master dev lane is removed, and a new dev-branch lane publishes DevNet releases from the d-inference `dev` branch. The same lane no longer uses the experimental ad-hoc, self-signed flow. Instead, release-dev-branch.yml calls the reusable release-provider.yml with `secrets: inherit` and gets Developer ID signing and notarization, so a dev build meets the self-updater's production designated requirement. The doc itself admits that `dev` has no pull_request review rule (head ~line 542) and that the source gate on master (`verify_workflow_source`) must be extended. That is the finding above. Other points noted: the doc says the dev lane reads only the shared Apple signing secrets plus `DEV_*` publication secrets, and that PROD_* and STAGING_* are guarded by environment conditions, pinned by scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py. The workflow YAML, resolve-provider-release.sh, provider_release_resume/api.py and the actual ruleset were not supplied, so these claims are unverified. The doc also notes a coordinator ReleaseVersionGreater non-SemVer ordering quirk, which is an availability and ordering issue with no direct security impact here. Open questions for the next pass: whether the build and sign jobs keep untrusted `dev` code away from signing secrets, whether the prod coordinator can ever receive a dev-branch registration, and whether the Developer ID signature with the shared keychain access group and APNs profile lets a dev build touch production-identity items.

findings.detail: The new Dev-Branch Lane section says a push to the d-inference `dev` branch calls `release-provider.yml` with `secrets: inherit` and gets the same Developer ID signature as master and prod builds. Such a build satisfies the self-updater's `DarkbloomCodeSignature` production requirement and the fan-helper requirement in `scripts/install.sh`. The same section states that review is not enforced on `dev`: the only protections are required signatures and a ref-creation bypass list. A single account on that bypass list, or a compromised one, could push unreviewed code. That code would be built, signed with the production Apple team identity (`SLDQ2GJ6TL`, bundle id `io.darkbloom.provider`), notarized and registered on the dev coordinator. Previously the branch lane used ad-hoc signing and a relaxed installer requirement. The doc says only the production registration and release key keep a dev build out of production, so the Developer ID signature is no longer a barrier. The lane is added with a documented missing control (a pull_request rule on `dev`). Fix: enforce the rule or an environment approval before enabling the lane, and update the threat model to cover the dev-branch signing path.
findings.title: Dev-branch pushes get production Developer ID signing, notarization and secrets while `dev` has no review rule
